thesis: Zscaler jumped about 17.7% to $229.30 (from $194.82) on 7.7x volume after agreeing on Nov 23 to be acquired by CrowdStrike in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9B (8-K): holders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, about $260.41 at CrowdStrike's Nov 20 close (a ~34% premium), and coverage reports the two stocks moved in opposite directions on the news. Both boards approved; founder Jay Chaudhry and affiliates (about 34% of shares) signed voting agreements; a breakup fee of about $1.4B could come due from Zscaler; closing requires stockholder approval, antitrust clearances and an effective S-4, and is expected in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028 (about late 2027 to early 2028). The shares now track CrowdStrike's stock and a long antitrust review rather than Zscaler's own results. The strongest plausible positive, the spread to the implied value closing, depends on that long regulatory path and on CrowdStrike's share price, so it isn't resolved. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation over the deal and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated, or the deal clears regulators early so the shares trade at the exchange ratio.

thesis: BILL Holdings edged up about 0.2% to $61.59 (from $61.44) on 3.2x volume, still pinned below the $63.25 per-share cash price in its Nov 19 agreement to be taken private by TPG with Corpay as minority partner (8-K): a 31% premium to the 60-day VWAP ending Nov 16, approved by the board, its largest holder Starboard and CEO René Lacerte, with closing expected in 1H 2027 subject to stockholder and other approvals. Corpay is taking about one-third for $1.1B with an option on the rest. With the price fixed, the remaining upside is a ~2.7% spread over several months, while a broken deal would expose the shares to their pre-report level. The strongest plausible positive, a competing bid, isn't ruled out, but this run found no go-shop, rival offer or lawsuit, and no restatement. Medium; avoid.
invalidation: A competing proposal above $63.25 emerges, or the merger agreement is terminated.

thesis: Kohl's fell about 4.7% to $21.20 (from $22.25) on 2.1x volume the day before its fiscal Q3 2026 report, confirmed for Nov 24 before the open; consensus is a loss of about $0.01 per share on revenue near $3.5B, down about 1.1%. thesis: BJ's Wholesale fell another 3.3% to $101.38 (from $104.82) on 2.0x volume, extending the drop after its Nov 20 fiscal Q3 2026 report. Analysts split today: BofA trimmed its target to $115 (Neutral) on tough margin comparisons next year, while TD Cowen raised to $122 (Buy) and DA Davidson to $123. The Nov 20 report beat (adjusted EPS of $1.73 vs. about $1.26 expected, comparable club sales ex-gas up 4.1%, membership fee income up 9.5%) and raised full-year guidance, but the quarter included a one-time pre-tax benefit from the interchange-fee litigation settlement disclosed in September, and merchandise margins contracted. A beat and raise flattered by a one-time gain, with margin pressure and split analyst reactions, makes the evidence mixed. The litigation check found the settled interchange case, a pension fund's securities suit dismissed by stipulation on May 6 after its proposal was included in the 2026 proxy, and no investigation or restatement. Low.
invalidation: Merchandise margins keep contracting, the raised EPS guide proves mostly one-time, or ex-gas comparable sales slow below the 2.5% floor.
sources: Investing.com (BofA cuts target on margin concerns): https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bofa-cuts-bjs-wholesale-stock-price-target-to-115-on-margin-concerns-93CH-5720610

thesis: Alliance Laundry rose about 6.1% to $25.74 (from $24.27) on 2.3x volume; this run found no company news dated today. The thesis rests on the Nov 10 Q3 2026 report: adjusted EPS of $0.38 beat the $0.32 consensus and full-year 2026 net revenue growth of 6-7% was reaffirmed, and analysts initiated with Buy or Outperform ratings on Nov 3. Counter-cases: guidance was reaffirmed, not raised; target changes after the print were mixed (Citi to $28 and Morgan Stanley to $29 up, JPMorgan to $31 and Baird to $30 down); and sponsor BDT still controls about 60.5% of the vote after selling 22.55M shares at $23.50 in an August secondary, which leaves an overhang of future sales. This run found only aggregator sources for the quarter, and today's move has no disclosed cause. The litigation check found only a 2024 plaintiff-firm data-breach solicitation, with no filed complaint or scheduled step found, and no restatement. Medium.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the reaffirmed 6-7% growth target, BDT launches another large secondary, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$24).
sources: Defense World (shares gap up on strong earnings, Nov 11): https://www.defenseworld.net/2026/11/11/alliance-laundry-nysealh-shares-gap-up-on-strong-earnings.html
